maintained_repo_url: https://github.com/BAI-LAB/MemoryOS (continuously maintained implementation repo from the authors' lab; includes a MemoryOS-MCP server integration; more current than the frozen EMNLP/arXiv PDF).
task_domain: Long-term conversational memory management for LLM-based AI agents / personalized dialogue agents (a QA + interactive personal-assistant setting). Evaluated on long multi-session dialogue QA, not on tool-use/embodied/code/decision-RL.
problem_setting: Interactive, single-agent setting with a FROZEN, off-the-shelf LLM (e.g. GPT-4o-mini; the LLM is prompted, not fine-tuned). The LLM's fixed context window is augmented by an OS-inspired hierarchical memory management system layered on top of the model. No task reward/supervision is used to train any component; all 'learning' is via LLM-prompted summarization/extraction plus off-the-shelf embedding similarity and heuristic heat scores. Memory is built up online over extended multi-session dialogues (LoCoMo conversations average ~300 turns / ~9K tokens; GVD spans simulated 10-day interactions). The agent must (a) retain dialogue history coherently across large temporal gaps and (b) maintain a persistent, evolving persona (user profile/traits/knowledge base + agent profile/traits) to give personalized, consistent answers. The four modules (Storage, Updating, Retrieval, Generation) run as a fixed pipeline; experiments use 8x H20 GPUs (only for serving/embeddings).
what_is_retrieved: experiences / memories: past dialogue pages (user query Q + model response R + timestamp T), LLM-summarized topic-segment summaries (mid-term), and persona/profile information (user profile, user traits across 90 dimensions, user knowledge base, agent profile, agent traits). These are retrieved from the agent's own growing memory store and injected into the generation prompt.
retrieval_grounding: GROWING / episodic memory the agent writes. The retrievable store is built entirely from the ongoing conversation (short-term dialogue pages -> mid-term topic segments -> long-term persona memory); there is no static external corpus/KB/API being queried. It is a self-written, online-growing personal memory (hence 'memory' rather than classic static-corpus RAG).
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Fixed top-k ranking (with a two-stage top-m then top-k cut), not a completeness/minimal-set objective. MTM retrieval selects top-m candidate segments then top-k dialogue pages within them; LPM retrieves top-10 entries from the User KB and Assistant Traits; STM returns all current dialogue pages. k is a fixed hyperparameter (top-m segments=5; top-k pages=5 on GVD, 10 on LoCoMo). No explicit minimal-needed-set or precision-driven variable-size objective.
cbr_cycle_coverage: [Retrieve: yes, Reuse: partial, Revise: no, Retain: yes]. MemoryOS Retrieves relevant memory tiers and Retains new dialogue/persona information (write-back across STM->MTM->LPM). 'Reuse' is only the injection of retrieved memory into the prompt (not case-solution adaptation); there is no CBR-style solution Revise step. (Approximate mapping; the work is not framed as CBR.)
explicit_cbr_grounding: False. MemoryOS does not frame itself as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner. It is explicitly framed as an OS-inspired memory operating system (segment-paging, FIFO, heat/LRU-style eviction, working-set models).
retrieval_unit: Multi-granular by tier: (a) STM = a 'dialogue page' = {Q_i, R_i, T_i, meta_chain_i} (one user-turn + model-response pair with timestamp and a chain meta-summary); (b) MTM = a 'segment' (an LLM-summarized topic cluster of multiple dialogue pages) at the first stage, then individual dialogue pages within the chosen segments at the second stage; (c) LPM = persona/profile entries (user profile fields, user-trait dimensions, User KB facts, agent profile/traits). The core retrievable units are dialogue pages and topic segments, plus persona entries.
index_source: Growing memory, online/test-time-induced. The store is constructed incrementally during the dialogue: STM pages are appended live, FIFO-migrated to MTM, clustered into LLM-summarized segments, and (when hot enough) distilled into LPM persona memory. Nothing is offline-induced from an external corpus; the entire index is built from the agent's own interaction stream.
index_structure_topology: Hierarchical, OS-style segment-paging. Three tiers: STM (fixed-length FIFO queue of dialogue pages, length 7) -> MTM (Segmented Paging: topic 'segments' each holding multiple dialogue 'pages'; max segment capacity 2000; each segment carries an embedding, keyword set, and heat score) -> LPM (structured persona store: User Profile/Static + User Traits [90 dims across 3 categories] + User KB [FIFO size 100] + Agent Profile + Agent Traits [FIFO size 100]). Within each tier retrieval uses flat embedding/Jaccard similarity; the topology across tiers is hierarchical (category->segment->page) plus heat-prioritized eviction, not a knowledge graph.
retriever_type: Dense embedding similarity + lexical (hybrid within MTM). Segment selection uses a combined score F_score = cos(e_s, e_p) + Jaccard(K_s, K_p) (semantic embedding cosine + keyword-set Jaccard). Page-level and LPM retrieval use semantic embedding (cosine) similarity / top-k semantic relevance. Off-the-shelf embeddings; no BM25 index per se, no learned/trained retriever, no generative tool-as-token retriever.
retriever_learning_signal: None (off-the-shelf / heuristic). Retrieval relies on frozen pretrained text-embedding similarity, LLM-generated keyword sets for Jaccard, fixed thresholds (segment similarity theta=0.6), and a hand-weighted heat score (alpha=beta=gamma=1). No contrastive training, no LM-feedback fine-tuning of the retriever, no downstream-task/preference optimization, no RL/value-based learning of the retrieval policy.
query_construction: Raw user query is the query/key. Given the current user query Q, MemoryOS embeds it and matches against segment/page/persona embeddings (and LLM-summarized keyword sets for MTM segment scoring). No sub-query decomposition, synthetic query expansion, or thought-conditioned query rewriting is described; the query is the user's current utterance.
query_granularity: Task/turn-level (one query per user turn, executed once per response), with a two-LEVEL retrieval within that turn for MTM (segment-level then page-level). It is not step/state-level inside a multi-step reasoning rollout; retrieval is performed once per dialogue turn before generation.
when_to_retrieve: One-shot per dialogue turn (fixed schedule). For every incoming user query the retrieval module is invoked once to gather STM + MTM (two-stage) + LPM context, then the generation module produces the response. No iterative/active/uncertainty-triggered or learned-router retrieval within a turn.
retrieval_trigger_signal: Fixed schedule: retrieval fires deterministically on each user turn (every query triggers a full STM/MTM/LPM retrieval pass before generation). There is no token-level confidence, attention/uncertainty signal, learned complexity classifier, reflection token, or agent-initiated request gating retrieval.
reranking: Two-stage hierarchical selection rather than a learned reranker. MTM first ranks segments by F_score (cosine + Jaccard) to pick top-m, then ranks dialogue pages within those segments by semantic similarity to pick top-k (a coarse-to-fine, hierarchy-aware selection). No cross-encoder, RRF, or instruction-tuned reranking model is used.
retrieved_context_refinement: Summarization/compression at storage time plus selection at query time; no query-time distillation/distractor-filtering module. Refinement is built into the storage hierarchy: dialogue chains are LLM-summarized into meta_chain; segments are LLM-summarized topic summaries; LPM stores distilled persona traits/facts. At retrieval, results are simply selected (top-m/top-k/top-10) and concatenated into the prompt; there is no separate reason-in-documents distillation or compression of the retrieved set beyond the per-tier selection cap.
tool_document_engineering: N/A. MemoryOS does not retrieve over tools/skills; no tool/skill descriptions are indexed.
index_content_separation: Partial / implicit. The MTM uses segment-level summaries/embeddings as a lightweight index that is matched first (top-m segments) before drilling into the heavier dialogue-page content (top-k pages within selected segments) - an index-then-content, progressive-disclosure pattern across the two-stage retrieval. It is not the SOP-index-then-content tool pattern, but the segment-summary-then-page-content design plays an analogous lightweight-index role.
dynamic_index_and_protocol: N/A. Not a tool-retrieval system (the repo ships a separate MemoryOS-MCP server to expose the memory system via MCP, but the paper itself does not retrieve over a live tool registry / RapidAPI / RESTful API store).
tool_dependency_awareness: N/A. No inter-tool dependency modeling (no tools/APIs are retrieved).
how_retrieved_used: Prompt augmentation. The Response Generation module integrates the retrieved STM (recent dialogue), MTM (relevant segment summaries + dialogue pages), and LPM (user profile/traits/KB + agent profile/traits) together with the current user query into a single final prompt fed to the frozen LLM, which generates a contextually coherent, personalized response. No training signal, skill execution, case adaptation, or latent-token injection - retrieved memory is consumed as in-context text.
planning_integration: Retrieve-then-generate (no explicit planning/search). MemoryOS is a fixed retrieve->prompt-assemble->generate pipeline per turn; there is no task planner, tree search/MCTS, hierarchical subtask decomposition, or interleaved plan-act loop. Retrieval interfaces with response generation, not with a planner.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: Per-answer (per dialogue turn). Retrieval is performed once and the result is used to produce the single response for that turn; retrieval is not woven per-CoT-step, per-sentence/token, or per-tool-call.
adaptation_mechanism: N/A (not a CBR case-adaptation system). Retrieved memory is injected verbatim/as-summarized into the prompt and the frozen LLM synthesizes the answer; there is no case-solution adaptation, execution-feedback revision, critic-guided revision, or RL reuse-finetuning. The closest 'adaptation' is the LLM-driven re-summarization/trait-extraction that happens when memory is promoted across tiers (a storage-side operation, not query-time case adaptation).
retrieved_item_representation: Mixed natural-language text: raw dialogue pages (Q/R/T), LLM-distilled chain meta-summaries and segment topic summaries, and structured persona fields/traits (User Profile fixed attributes, 90-dimension User Traits, User KB facts, Agent Profile/Traits). Injected as plain text into the prompt. No executable program/skill or latent/soft tokens.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Multi-level: raw dialogue turns (STM) -> distilled per-topic segment summaries (MTM) -> highly distilled, state-aware persona traits/profile/knowledge (LPM). So retrieval spans raw trajectory-like dialogue, distilled topic summaries, and distilled persona 'insight'/preference representations simultaneously.
noise_robustness_mechanism: Topic-coherent segmentation + capped retrieval breadth, rather than a learned relevance filter. Pages are merged into a segment only if F_score exceeds threshold theta=0.6, keeping segments topically coherent and reducing cross-topic contamination (the paper criticizes MemGPT's flat FIFO for 'topic mixing'). The two-stage segment-then-page retrieval narrows the candidate pool. The hyperparameter analysis explicitly notes that retrieving too many pages 'may introduce noise, adversely affecting performance', motivating k=10. No retriever-aware training, self-reflection relevance evaluator, reason-in-documents refinement, or distractor-aware SFT.
memory_type: Episodic + procedural/persona memory in an OS-inspired three-tier hierarchy: Short-Term Memory (STM, FIFO queue of dialogue pages), Mid-Term Memory (MTM, segment-paging topic store), and Long-term Personal Memory (LPM, structured user/agent persona = profile + traits + knowledge base). Long-term, persistent, self-managed, single-agent private.
write_back: True. MemoryOS continuously writes new experiences into memory: every dialogue turn is appended as an STM page (with LLM-generated chain meta); FIFO-evicted STM pages are written into MTM segments (with LLM topic summarization); hot MTM segments are distilled into LPM (User Traits/User KB/Agent Traits). Write-back is core to the system.
online_growth: Yes. The memory store grows continuously during deployment/test time across the multi-session dialogue: STM appends turns, MTM accumulates and re-summarizes segments, and LPM evolves persona traits/knowledge. Capacity is bounded by FIFO/heat eviction rather than frozen after an offline induction phase.
write_back_trigger: Per-step / scheduled cascade, not success/failure-conditioned. (1) STM write: every dialogue turn is appended as a page (per-step). (2) STM->MTM: triggered when the STM FIFO queue (length 7) overflows - the oldest page migrates to MTM. (3) MTM eviction: segments exceeding capacity (max 2000) are evicted by lowest heat (heat = alpha*N_visit + beta*L_interaction + gamma*R_recency, with R_recency an exponential time decay). (4) MTM->LPM: segments whose heat exceeds threshold F=5 are promoted to LPM (persona trait/KB extraction; then L_interaction reset to 0 to decay heat and avoid redundancy). No task-reward / on-success-vs-failure gating; writes are driven by FIFO position, heat, and recency.
failure_experience_usage: N/A in the success/failure sense. There is no task-level success/failure label; all dialogue turns are stored uniformly. The system does not store failed vs successful experiences contrastively or maintain failure-only corrective rules - it is a conversational memory store, not an experience-of-failures learner.
memory_evolution_update: Mixed: append-then-summarize / dedup-by-merge / refine-overwrite / forget-prune. STM is append-only within its FIFO window (then forget-from-STM via FIFO eviction to MTM). MTM merges topically similar pages into the same segment (dedup/cluster-merge, threshold theta=0.6) and re-summarizes segment content via LLM; segments are forget-pruned by lowest-heat eviction at capacity. LPM persona traits/KB are incrementally extracted and updated (refine/overwrite of evolving traits), with User KB and Agent Traits maintained as fixed-size FIFO queues (size 100). After MTM->LPM promotion, the segment's L_interaction is reset to 0 (heat decay) to prevent repeated promotion/redundancy. The paper's Limitations note the lack of dynamic segment-merging to resolve overlapping/evolving topics.
retrieval_as_learned_policy: No. Retrieval and memory promotion/eviction are governed by fixed similarity thresholds, top-m/top-k cutoffs, and a hand-weighted heat/recency heuristic (alpha=beta=gamma=1; F=5; theta=0.6) - not a learned or RL-optimized retrieval/selection policy (no M-MDP, soft Q-learning, or trained selector).
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: No. Single-agent private memory: each MemoryOS instance maintains its own user/agent persona and dialogue memory. No cross-agent or cross-framework memory/experience sharing is proposed.
benchmarks: (1) LoCoMo benchmark (Maharana et al., 2024) - very long-term conversational memory, ultra-long dialogues averaging ~300 turns / ~9K tokens; questions in four categories: Single-hop, Multi-hop, Temporal, Open-domain; scored by F1 and BLEU-1. (2) GVD dataset (Zhong et al., 2024, the MemoryBank evaluation set) - multi-turn dialogues simulated between 15 virtual users and an assistant over a 10-day period, >=2 topics/day; scored by Memory Retrieval Accuracy (binary), Response Correctness, and Contextual Coherence (3-point scale), auto-judged by DeepSeek-R1.
benchmark_family: memory / long-term conversational memory (LoCoMo, the canonical LoCoMo/LongMemEval-style family) plus a personalized-dialogue memory set (GVD from MemoryBank). QA-flavored multi-session dialogue memory; not web/embodied/tool/code/decision-RL families.
baselines: TiM (Think-in-Memory; Liu et al., 2023), MemoryBank (Zhong et al., 2024), MemGPT (Packer et al., 2023), A-Mem (Agentic Memory; Xu et al., 2025), and a plain base LLM (GPT-4o-mini, no memory). On LoCoMo, A-Mem is reported both as the original paper's numbers and as a re-implementation (A-Mem*) under the same environment.
key_metrics: LoCoMo: F1 and BLEU-1 (per-category Single-hop / Multi-hop / Temporal / Open-domain, plus average ranks). GVD: Memory Retrieval Accuracy (Acc., binary 0/1), Response Correctness (Corr., 0/0.5/1), Contextual Coherence (Cohe., 0/0.5/1), auto-scored by DeepSeek-R1.
headline_result: On the LoCoMo benchmark with GPT-4o-mini as the base LLM, MemoryOS yields an average improvement of 49.11% in F1 and 46.18% in BLEU-1 over the baselines (the single most-cited headline figure, stated in the abstract). MemoryOS attains the best (rank 1.0) average F1/BLEU-1 ranking across the four LoCoMo question categories. [uncertain] exact per-category absolute F1/BLEU-1 cells are partly garbled by PDF/OCR in the scraped Table 2, so individual cell values are not transcribed verbatim here.
ablations: Component ablations (Figure 2) remove: the Persona/Long-Term module (-LPM), the Dialogue-page Chain (-Chain), the Mid-Term Memory (-MTM), and the entire system (-MemoryOS). Findings: removing the memory system entirely (-MemoryOS) causes the largest performance drop; among components, MTM has the most significant impact, followed by LPM, while the dialogue-page Chain has the least impact. Hyperparameter analysis (Figure 3) on LoCoMo varies top-k MTM dialogue pages over k in {5,10,20,30,40}: performance rises with k but with diminishing returns and eventual noise; k=10 chosen as the favorable accuracy/cost trade-off.
evaluation_decoupling: Partial. On GVD an intrinsic memory metric (Memory Retrieval Accuracy, binary) is reported separately from the end-to-end response-quality metrics (Correctness, Coherence). On LoCoMo only end-to-end QA metrics (F1, BLEU-1) are reported - no separate Recall@k/nDCG retrieval metric. So intrinsic-vs-end-to-end decoupling exists only on GVD and is coarse (binary retrieval accuracy, not Recall@k/nDCG).
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Mostly outcome metrics (F1, BLEU-1, response correctness). Some process/quality signal is captured: GVD's Memory Retrieval Accuracy probes whether the right memory was recalled, and Contextual Coherence judges dialogue-flow quality beyond raw answer correctness; the LoCoMo per-category breakdown (single/multi-hop/temporal/open-domain) gives reasoning-type-resolved outcome scores. No step-wise retrieval-accuracy or reasoning-faithfulness metric within a turn.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Discussed qualitatively / via k-sweep rather than a full cost table. The hierarchical segment-paging + heat-based eviction is argued to be more efficient than alternatives (the paper notes A-Mem's heavy multi-step link generation 'inflates latency and error accumulation', and MemGPT's flat FIFO causes topic mixing). The top-k analysis picks k=10 to 'minimize computational overhead' while retaining most of the accuracy gain (larger k adds noise and cost). No explicit per-query token-cost, dollar-cost, or latency-vs-accuracy table is reported.
context_budget_and_selection_count: Fixed-k, budget-capped selection. STM is a length-7 FIFO of dialogue pages (all returned). MTM retrieval is two-stage with fixed cutoffs: top-m segments=5, then top-k dialogue pages=5 (GVD) / 10 (LoCoMo). LPM returns top-10 entries each from User KB and Assistant Traits plus all profile/trait fields. Memory capacities are capped (MTM segment max 2000; User KB / Agent Traits FIFO size 100) with heat/FIFO eviction governing what stays. k is a tuned constant (k=10 on LoCoMo), not adaptive/precision-driven.
benchmark_construction_and_size: N/A (MemoryOS is a method, not a benchmark). For context on the datasets it uses: LoCoMo (Maharana et al., 2024) is a human/LLM-curated very-long-term-conversation benchmark (~300 turns, ~9K tokens per conversation; four QA categories); GVD (Zhong et al., 2024) is an LLM-simulated dialogue set (15 virtual users x ~10 days, >=2 topics/day), answer quality auto-judged by DeepSeek-R1.
builds_on: Operating-systems segment-paging and virtual-memory management (Multics segment-page memory, Bensoussan et al. 1972; virtual memory / working-set & LRU eviction, Denning 1970; segment-page management on many-core processors, Zheng et al. 2020); MemGPT's OS-style hierarchical read/write memory (Packer et al. 2023); prior LLM-agent memory systems for long dialogue - MemoryBank's vector memory + Ebbinghaus forgetting curve and the GVD dataset (Zhong et al. 2024), Think-in-Memory (Liu et al. 2023), A-Mem agentic note network (Xu et al. 2025), Generative Agents memory+reflection (Park et al. 2023), Self-Controlled Memory (Wang et al. 2025); psychological memory-recall-inspired two-stage retrieval (Yuan et al. 2024); 90-dimension user-trait personalization (Li et al. 2025); LoCoMo evaluation (Maharana et al. 2024).
contrasts_with: MemGPT (OS-style paging but a FLAT FIFO queue that causes topic mixing as dialogue grows - MemoryOS adds topic-segment paging + hierarchy); A-Mem (interconnected note graph that enriches semantics but whose heavy multi-step link generation inflates latency and error accumulation); MemoryBank (forgetting-curve decay alone, found insufficient and weakest baseline); Think-in-Memory (single-stage LSH hash retrieval that cannot preserve cross-topic dependencies). More broadly, MemoryOS positions itself against single-dimension memory methods (knowledge-organization vs retrieval-mechanism vs architecture-driven) by unifying storage + updating + retrieval + generation into one system.
lineage: Group F (decision / memory / RL): the long-term / episodic-memory-management lineage of retrieval-augmented LLM agents. Directly extends the OS-inspired hierarchical-memory line opened by MemGPT, adding a three-tier STM/MTM/LPM architecture with topic segment-paging, dialogue-chain FIFO, heat/recency (LRU-style) eviction, and an evolving persona module. Sits alongside MemoryBank, A-Mem, Think-in-Memory, and Generative Agents as a long-term conversational/personalized-memory system, and has itself become a baseline/target in subsequent memory-retrieval work (e.g., HiNS, 2026).
